Created (all compile clean with `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic`, no headers edited, no new prototypes):

- `/workspace/src/common/crc32_table.c` — `xr_crc32_table[8][256]`, machine-generated by a throwaway program (`/tmp/gen/gentab.c`); the recurrence is documented in `crc32.c` so it can be regenerated.
- `/workspace/src/common/crc64_table.c` — `xr_crc64_table[4][256]`.
- `/workspace/src/common/crc32.c` — slice-by-8, `/workspace/src/common/crc64.c` — slice-by-4. Both align to 4 bytes first, complement internally, init 0.
- `/workspace/src/common/sha256.c` — FIPS 180-4; the block buffer is `check->buffer.u8` with the fill position derived from `size & 63`, digest written big-endian over `buffer.u8[0..31]`.
- `/workspace/src/common/check.c` — dispatch plus `xr_check_sizes[16]` = spec table; CRC32/CRC64 stored little-endian at finish.

Verification: CRC32("123456789")=0xCBF43926, CRC64=0x995DC9BBDF1939FA; SHA-256 matches all four FIPS vectors ("", "abc", the 56-byte two-block message fed one byte at a time, 1M 'a'); tables match a bit-by-bit reference over 2000 random buffers at every alignment.

Against `/workspace/executable`: for a 28-byte file and a 300 KB random file, the bytes I produce equal the stored check in `-C crc32/crc64/sha256` output exactly (e.g. 28-byte file, crc64 `1d ef 25 1c 38 79 a6 7f` at offset 64; sha256 `132b554a...afe0` at 64..95). Stream header CRC32 over Stream Flags (`00 04` -> `e6 d6 b4 46`, `00 0a` -> `e1 fb 0c a1`) and the footer CRC32 (`1f b6 f3 7d`) also match.
